commit.subject: feat(models): remote model catalog manifest for OpenRouter + Nous Portal (#16033)
commit.body_excerpt:
OpenRouter and Nous Portal curated picker lists now resolve via a JSON
manifest served by the docs site, falling back to the in-repo snapshot
when unreachable. Lets us update model lists without shipping a release.

Live URL: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/api/model-catalog.json
(source at website/static/api/model-catalog.json; auto-deploys via the
existing deploy-site.yml GitHub Pages pipeline on every merge to main).

Schema (v1) carries id + optional description + free-form metadata at
manifest, provider, and model levels. Pricing and context length stay
live-fetched via existing machinery (/v1/models endpoints, models.dev).

Config (new model_catalog section, default enabled):
  model_catalog.url       master manifest URL
  model_catalog.ttl_hours disk cache TTL (default 24h)
  model_catalog.providers.<name>.url   optional per-provider override

Fetch pipeline: in-process cache -> disk cache (fresh < TTL) -> HTTP
fetch -> disk-cache-on-failure fallback -> in-repo snapshot as last
resort. Never raises to callers; at worst returns the bundled list.

Changes:
- website/static/api/model-catalog.json    initial manifest (35 OR + 31 Nous)
- scripts/build_model_catalog.py

evidence_units.claim: The pinned implementation commit states that curated OpenRouter and Nous picker lists now resolve through a hosted JSON manifest, with cache and bundled-list fallbacks so lists can change without a CLI release.

The change adds a schema-versioned manifest with provider blocks, model identifiers, optional descriptions, and free-form metadata, plus a generator that converts the bundled curated lists into that format.
The default configuration enables remote catalog resolution, defines the master URL and 24-hour TTL, and provides a map for per-provider URL overrides.

The catalog loader rejects non-object manifests, missing or unsupported versions, malformed provider blocks, non-list model collections, and model entries without non-empty string identifiers; HTTP, decoding, validation, and I/O failures return no remote manifest instead of escaping to callers.

Catalog resolution uses a fresh disk-backed in-process cache when possible, fetches when forced or stale, writes fetched data through a temporary file and os.replace, returns stale validated disk data after fetch failure, and otherwise returns an empty catalog for higher-level bundled fallback.

Provider resolution optionally fetches a provider-specific manifest first, falls back to the master catalog, and adapts provider blocks into the pre-existing OpenRouter tuple shape or Nous identifier-list shape; empty or unavailable data is represented as None.

OpenRouter now uses remotely resolved tuples when available and otherwise OPENROUTER_MODELS, then retains its existing live availability, tool-capability, pricing, and recommended-model processing. The Nous adapter similarly returns remote identifiers when non-empty and otherwise a copy of the bundled list.

commit.subject: Refresh the model catalog before turns after auth changes (#46508)
commit.body_excerpt:
## Why

Credential changes can leave the in-memory model catalog associated with a different identity, causing subsequent turns to use bundled model metadata instead of the active credentials' catalog.

## What changed

- Refresh mismatched catalogs before user turns and mailbox-triggered wakeups, resolving lazy command credentials before comparing identities.
- Reuse a matching cache or fetch models with a five-second deadline covering auth resolution and cache access. Preserve fallback behavior on failure or timeout; static catalogs need no refresh.
- Recheck the active turn after discovery so an interrupted wakeup does not continue starting a turn.

## Testing

Add coverage for user and mailbox turns after credential rotation, including switching back after another identity replaces the shared catalog. Verify refreshed context windows and request behavior, fallback on discovery failure or auth timeout, and command-auth token rotation.

commit.subject: fix(core): add kimi-k3 token limits (1M context, 128K output) (#7144)
commit.body_excerpt:
Kimi K3 exposes a 1M-token context window and defaults max output to
128K. Without explicit rules it fell through to the generic Kimi
fallback (256K context) and the default output limit, which would
trigger context compaction far too early and under-size the output
budget. Register explicit context-window and output rules so token
accounting matches the model, and mirror them into the
vscode-ide-companion token-limit table.

workflow_graph.goal: Make every in-scope token-limit resolver return the documented input and output capacities for a newly distinguished model generation without regressing older family mappings.
when_to_use: A recognized model generation is being classified by a broader family rule or a global default instead of its documented capabilities.
The repository has an ordered capability catalog and one or more isolated consumers that intentionally mirror it.
anti_goals: Do not change token-limit lookup, normalization, compaction, or request-clamping algorithms when correcting catalog metadata is sufficient.
Do not replace or widen the broad family fallback, because older or unknown family members must retain their established behavior.
Do not treat the provider's maximum configurable output as the default output value when the documented default is lower.
not_applicable_when: The model identifier is already supplied with authoritative runtime metadata that always bypasses the static fallback catalog.
The required capability values or identifier matching boundary cannot be established from authoritative documentation.
The secondary consumer can import and use the authoritative catalog directly and therefore has no independent mirror to reconcile.
inputs: A stable model identifier or identifier pattern
Documented input context capacity
Documented default output capacity
The authoritative ordered capability table
Any environment-isolated mirror tables
Existing family and global fallback expectations
workflow_graph.entry_state: The target generation falls through to less-specific metadata in at least one resolver, producing an incorrect input capacity, output capacity, or both.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Specific rules precede broader fallbacks in the authoritative catalog, every required isolated mirror agrees with it, and direct lookup checks prove both the new values and unchanged legacy fallback behavior.

steps.condition: Use when verified model capabilities differ from the currently matched family or global fallback.

validation_ladder: Inspect rule ordering to confirm the specific identifier is tested before the broad family fallback in every input table.
Probe authoritative input and output lookup results for the target identifier.
Probe an existing family identifier to detect unintended fallback changes.
Run the same probes against each isolated mirror and compare results.
Add and run explicit regression tests for the new identifier in both modes; this final rung is deferred because commit 945cf3c8 added no such tests and the bundle contains no status-check evidence.
stop_conditions: Stop if the capability values are unverified or distinguish maximum configurable output from default output ambiguously.
Stop if normalization transforms the proposed identifier so the new rule cannot match as intended.
Stop if a required isolated consumer has different lookup semantics that cannot be reconciled by equivalent metadata entries.
Do not claim full automated validation until target-specific regression assertions or equivalent status-check evidence exist.
